verdict: READY TO MERGE - 15 of 15 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: test_help_links.py is fully behavioral: it builds real .atbx zips (BOM variants, stored/deflated members, fixed timestamps) and runs swap_atbx_links unstubbed, asserting exact member bytes rather than substrings.
Refusal tests pin the all-or-nothing contract with _assert_untouched (same bytes and no leftover temp file), including the read-only os.replace and failed-testzip write paths.

Discriminating edge cases: page on disk but not shipped (proves the shipped set, not the filesystem, is consulted), prose 'file:' text, URL-encoded and case-differing tails, links already at the release prefix, foreign drive and UNC hrefs.
test_prod_deploy_help_links.py is an end-to-end test over a real git checkout and the real fpm.json, and asserts the source archive bytes never change in real or dry runs.
The two monkeypatches (swap_atbx_links raising, ZipFile.testzip failing) are fault injection on collaborators with outcome assertions, not mock-chain wiring.
test_stale_dest_file_does_not_satisfy_a_link and test_link_to_a_denied_source_file_fails first establish the tempting file exists, so a regression to an on-disk check would fail them.

help_links.py writes through a mkstemp temp beside the archive, validates it (testzip plus re-decode of changed members) and os.replace's it, so any failure leaves the original archive untouched as the module docstring promises.
All-or-nothing rule is enforced in one place: swap_atbx_links writes only when apply, swap_count > 0, no missing targets and no errors, matching the LinkSwapResult and module docstrings.
Members are re-encoded with the byte-order mark and encoding they were read with, and non-scanned members, order, timestamps and archive comment are carried over.

LinkSwap.for_paths uses Path.as_uri for both prefixes, so drive and UNC roots produce the same percent-encoded form, and _missing_targets unquotes tails before a case-insensitive comparison against shipped paths.
Swap errors stay contained per archive: _swap_archive converts any scan exception into an error string, so the debug-override result and other archives still report normally.

_load_paths computes the release folder once and applies it to both dest_root and help_root; an empty HELP_ROOT maps to None, and the defaulted help_root keeps two-field ProjectPaths constructions valid.

The _copy_folder early return for an absent source folder turns a FileNotFoundError traceback for required:false folders into a clean skip, with validate_source still refusing absent required folders.
Every decision (D1-D4) records the question with code citations, all rejected options, the chosen option and the dated developer amendment, so the D1 non-UNC error rule is traceable to its origin.
Anchors spot-checked against the merge-base tree (prod_deploy.py:53, 58-69, 107-110, 118-127, 423-424, 432-433) match exactly; the frozen tree equals the merge base tree.
Sweeps enumerate every ProjectPaths/CopyResult/ProdCopier consumer with the compatibility reasoning, and the code honors it: help_root defaults to None and CopyResult stays four fields.

TASK-4's hook contract (top-level .atbx selection, single ValueError error, per-archive exception wrapping, error string shapes, D2 patched rule, read-only source scan in a dry run) matches conversion/prod_deploy.py _swap_help_links/_swap_archive line for line.
The PIP is a faithful render of the JSON: decisions, values, formats, sweeps and test node lists agree between the two files.

help_links.py rewrites all or nothing: it writes a temp zip beside the archive, validates it with testzip and decodes the changed members, then os.replace. Any failure leaves the original byte-identical with no temp file, and tests cover the read-only and failed-validation cases.

The shipped set is built from ProdCopier's copied list, not from what is on disk, so a stale dest file or a denied source page cannot satisfy a link. tests/test_prod_deploy_help_links.py pins both with real git checkouts.

The tests are genuinely behavioral: they build real .atbx zips (BOM variants, stored and deflated members, directory entries) and compare members byte for byte. The only monkeypatches inject faults; none checks wiring.
D4 fixes a real crash: an absent required: false folder used to raise FileNotFoundError out of run. It now has a guard at prod_deploy.py:380-381 and real and dry-run tests.
ProjectPaths.help_root defaults to None, so every existing positional two-field construction keeps working, and a test pins that.

important.name: Plan copies of the test modules are collectable by a bare pytest run
important.summary:
The PR commits four test_*.py files under docs/PLANS/0001/tests/tests/ (no __init__.py, no conftest), and pyproject.toml has no [tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths or norecursedirs. A `pytest` run from the repo root therefore walks docs/ before tests/ and collects these copies as top-level modules (test_help_links, test_prod_deploy_help_links, ...). Under `python -m pytest` they run a second time next to tests/ (and the help-links copy is a stale subset, see the next finding); under the console-script `pytest` the docs modules are imported before tests/conftest.py puts the repo root on sys.path, so `from conversion...` can fail with a collection error. Either way the plan fixtures leak into the suite.

Also (roast): This PR adds four tracked test modules under docs/PLANS/0001/tests/tests/ (no __init__.py), and pyproject.toml has no [tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths or norecursedirs. A bare `pytest` from the repo root collects docs/ before tests/. With the pytest entry script (e.g. `uv run pytest`, package = false so `conversion` is not installed), the cwd is not on sys.path and the repo root only joins it once the tests/ package is imported, so the four docs modules fail collection with ModuleNotFoundError: conversion. With `python -m pytest`, they import fine but every help-link test runs twice, and the docs copy of test_help_links.py is already stale (it lacks the two tests at tests/test_help_links.py:289-304). Before this PR, tests/ was the only test tree and a bare run was clean. The planning scaffold now gets into the suite.
fix: Add `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` with `testpaths = ["tests"]` to pyproject.toml so only tests/ is collected.
Or add `norecursedirs = ["docs", ...]` to the pytest options in pyproject.toml.
Or rename the plan copies to a non-collected suffix (e.g. test_help_links.py.txt) and update the copy steps in docs/PLANS/0001_Help_link_swap_PIP.md lines 81, 120, 152 and 226.
Add `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` with `testpaths = ["tests"]` to pyproject.toml so only tests/ is collected by default.
Or add `norecursedirs = ["docs", ".*", "build", "dist", "venv"]` under `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` in pyproject.toml.

minor.name: swap_atbx_links Args describe a narrower contract than the caller uses
minor.summary: The docstring says 'atbx: The copied archive to rewrite in place' and 'shipped: Repo-relative posix paths of the files the release ships'. prod_deploy._swap_archive passes the source archive (read-only, apply=False) in a dry run, and builds shipped relative to dest_root (release-relative), which is also the base the link tails are compared against (tails follow new_prefix, i.e. the release folder).
fix: Reword the Args: 'atbx: The archive to scan; rewritten in place only when apply is True' and 'shipped: Posix paths, relative to the release folder (dest_root), of the files the release ships'.

minor.name: Docs present DEST_ROOT as a working fallback, but a non-UNC target always fails
minor.summary: prod_deploy.py:7 calls HELP_ROOT optional, and prod_deploy.py:17-19 says links are swapped "to HELP_ROOT, else DEST_ROOT". fpm.env:6 likewise opens with "Optional:". But help_links.py:167-173 (D1) makes any swap onto a non-UNC prefix an error. The tracked fpm.env has a local DEST_ROOT and HELP_ROOT commented out, and the live archive holds one link (PIP Values row 28). So every real run.py deploy with the shipped config now ends with that error and exit 1 until someone sets HELP_ROOT. The behavior is the accepted D1 design. The docstrings just make it sound like a working fallback.
fix: prod_deploy.py:17-20: add that a swapped link pointing at a non-UNC prefix is an error, so a local DEST_ROOT needs a UNC HELP_ROOT once the archive holds a help link.
fpm.env:6: replace 'Optional:' with wording such as 'Required once the archive holds help links (DEST_ROOT is local):'.

minor.name: Dry-run patched semantics not stated in ProdCopier and _swap_archive docstrings
minor.summary:
The ProdCopier class docstring (lines 304-305) says 'an archive swapped without error joins patched', and _swap_archive (line 484) says 'swapped is True when the result is ok with links swapped'. In a dry run nothing is swapped (apply=False on the source archive), yet _swap_archive returns True and the dest path joins CopyResult.patched as the would-be path (plan D2, asserted by test_dry_run_checks_the_source_and_writes_nothing). The debug-override step adds nothing to patched in a dry run, so a reader of the docstrings gets the opposite of what dry-run patched holds for archives.

Also (roast): prod_deploy.py:304-305 says "an archive swapped without error joins patched". Under D2, _swap_archive (prod_deploy.py:487-494) also adds the would-be dest path in a dry run, where nothing is swapped or even copied. This is the opposite of _patch_debug_override, which reports nothing in a dry run (prod_deploy.py:437-438). Anyone reading the class docstring will expect patched to stay empty on a dry run.
fix: Extend the class docstring: 'an archive swapped without error joins patched; in a dry run, an archive that would be swapped joins patched as its dest path', and reword _swap_archive's Returns line to 'swapped is True when the result is ok with at least one link to swap (written in a real run, would-be in a dry run)'.
prod_deploy.py:304-305: append 'in a dry run, an archive whose source scan is ok with links to swap joins patched as its would-be dest path (D2).'

minor.name: ProjectPaths.help_root semantics undocumented; LinkSwap.for_paths names env keys instead
minor.summary: ProjectPaths.help_root (project_model.py:17) carries HELP_ROOT with the release folder already appended by _load_paths (prod_deploy.py:74), and LinkSwap.for_paths uses it directly as the link prefix. Neither the dataclass nor for_paths states this: for_paths' docstring reads 'SOURCE_ROOT -> HELP_ROOT, else DEST_ROOT', so a caller building ProjectPaths by hand with help_root=Path(HELP_ROOT) (no release folder) gets links one level too high and every target reported missing.
fix: Add a field comment on ProjectPaths.help_root: 'HELP_ROOT / <release folder>; prefix for swapped help links only, None falls back to dest_root', and reword the for_paths docstring to 'source_root -> help_root (HELP_ROOT plus the release folder), else dest_root'.

That change, plus two tests (tests/test_help_links.py: test_link_already_at_the_release_prefix_is_checked, test_shipped_link_already_at_the_release_prefix_is_ok), landed after the sealed records: neither the TASK-3 tree 9e038a5 nor the TASK-4 tree cdfff33 contains them (git grep finds no 'linked'/'already_at_the_release_prefix' there). Both tasks are COMPLETE, but neither evidence nor notes says when or how the gate passed, so the merged plan cannot show the precondition was met.
